passage: When the neighbours came up to their Mumbai flat, Lalremsiami, two, slid behind Damini's legs and looked at the floor. The neighbour crouched and said, "Hello, Lalremsiami!" She went quiet and gripped the hem of Damini's kurta. Damini said, "She likes to watch first." She offered the visitor a seat and chatted. After some minutes Lalremsiami crept out and held up her toy giraffe to the neighbour.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do when the neighbour said hello?
qa.a: She went quiet and gripped the hem of Damini's kurta.

qa.q: What does Lalremsiami's hiding behind Damini suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests shyness with people she does not know well. She might also have been tired.

qa.q: What did Damini do well?
qa.a: She gave Lalremsiami time to watch and warm up and did not force a greeting.

qa.q: How might the neighbour feel about the wait?
qa.a: She might feel unsure at first, but the giraffe shows Lalremsiami has decided she is welcome.

grounding: A toddler hides behind a parent with strangers, and shyness improves with gentle warm-up time, not pushing.

passage:
"Noor, say hello to Auntie."
Noor tucked behind Hafsa's knees.
"That's okay," said Hafsa. "Noor is watching first."
"Hello, Noor," said Auntie softly. "I like your yellow shoes."
Noor peeked.
"Yellow," she whispered.
"Yes. Yellow."
Hafsa sat on the sofa and Noor came out, still near her, and showed her shoes to Auntie.

qa.q: What did Auntie notice about Noor?
qa.a: She noticed Noor's yellow shoes.

qa.q: What does Noor's whispering yellow suggest about her feelings, and what else might it show?
qa.a: It suggests she is warming up and starting to trust Auntie. It might also be pride in her shoes.

qa.q: What worked in this scene?
qa.a: Hafsa did not push, and Auntie talked about something Noor could look at safely. 🙂

qa.q: How might Noor have felt if she had been forced to hug Auntie?
qa.a: She might feel unsafe and become more withdrawn, and the visit would start badly.

grounding: A toddler hides behind a parent or goes quiet with strangers, and shyness improves with warm-up time, not pushing.

passage: Daycare note, first week. Ishita hid behind her father's legs every morning this week and looked away whenever I said hello. I didn't push her to greet me. On Monday and Tuesday she sat on his lap and watched. On Wednesday she took a crayon from the table. On Friday she let go of his hand and sat beside me at the play dough. Sharmila, daycare teacher

qa.q: What did Ishita do on Friday?
qa.a: She let go of her father's hand and sat beside Sharmila at the play dough.

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling at the start of the week?
qa.a: She felt shy and unsure with a new teacher and place.

qa.q: What helped Ishita warm up over the week?
qa.a: Sharmila didn't push her to greet, and her father stayed while she watched and came closer at her own pace.

qa.q: How might Ishita's father feel by Friday?
qa.a: He would likely feel relieved and proud to see her join in.

grounding: A teacher gives a shy toddler warm-up time instead of pushing, and she joins in by the end of the week.

passage:
At the village wedding, Shalini hid behind her mother's sari when all the relatives crowded round. Her aunt Ritu didn't reach for her. She sat on the floor a little way off and rolled a small ball gently toward Shalini's feet.
Shalini looked at it, then at Ritu, then away. Ritu waited. After a long moment, a small foot came out from behind the sari and pushed the ball back.

qa.q: What did Ritu roll toward Shalini?
qa.a: A small ball.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling as she hid behind the sari?
qa.a: She was shy and overwhelmed with so many relatives crowding round.

qa.q: Which of Ritu's choices helped Shalini warm up?
qa.a: Sitting a little way off and rolling a ball without reaching for her, then waiting.

qa.q: How might Ritu feel when the small foot pushes the ball back?
qa.a: She would likely feel pleased and touched by the small step. 🙂

grounding: An aunt helps a shy toddler warm up with a gentle game instead of pushing her.

passage:
The new neighbour, Rania, came to the door of the Istanbul flat with a plate of pastries. Elif went quiet, looked at the floor and stood behind her mother.
Rania didn't bend down or ask for a hello. She sat and chatted with Elif's mother over tea.
Half an hour later, Elif walked over and put a biscuit on Rania's saucer, without a word.

qa.q: What did Rania bring?
qa.a: A plate of pastries.

qa.q: What was Elif feeling when she looked at the floor?
qa.a: She was shy and unsure with a new person.

qa.q: What did Rania do that helped Elif?
qa.a: She didn't push for a greeting and gave Elif time to warm up.

qa.q: How might Rania feel when Elif offers the biscuit?
qa.a: She would probably feel touched and pleased by the quiet gesture.

grounding: A new neighbour gives a shy toddler warm-up time, and the child approaches in her own way.

passage:
I'm Rajni from across the lane. At the Eid lunch, little Farida came in holding her Ammi's hand, took one look at the room full of people and hid behind her.
“Come, beta, say salaam to everyone!” the aunties called.
Farida looked at the floor and didn't make a sound.
Her Ammi just sat down with her on the carpet. “She'll come when she's ready.”
Later I saw Farida slip out, take a sweet from my plate, and smile at me.

qa.q: What did Farida take from Rajni's plate?
qa.a: She took a sweet.

qa.q: What was Farida feeling when she hid behind her Ammi and looked at the floor?
qa.a: She was shy and uneasy with so many people, needing time to feel comfortable.

qa.q: Why was her Ammi's approach better than the aunties' calls?
qa.a: Giving Farida time to warm up next to her helped her feel safe, while pushing her to greet everyone could make her shyer.

qa.q: How did the aunties seem to see Farida's silence?
qa.a: They seemed to expect a greeting and kept calling for her to say salaam.

grounding: It illustrates a shy toddler hiding behind a parent and going quiet with strangers, and gentle warm-up time working better than pushing.
